summary: A full-size scene photographed as if it were a tabletop model: high telephoto camera, a narrow horizontal band of sharp focus, lifted saturation and hard small-scale sun.
objective: A single horizontal sharp band covering 18-25% of frame height contains the hero, and blur increases monotonically toward the top and bottom edges of the frame.
intent_signals: Make it look like a tilt-shift miniature
Diorama photo of a city block from above
Shoot the scene like a tabletop model
example_prompts: A tilt-shift view of a harbour loading yard so it reads as a tabletop model.
Miniature-looking city intersection seen from a high telephoto camera with a narrow band of focus.

principles: The illusion is optical, not geometric: the scene may be full-size and correctly proportioned, and the miniature read comes entirely from focus falloff, camera height and colour lift.

Triangulate three traits shared by fake-miniature photographs — (a) a high, steeply-pitched telephoto viewpoint, (b) a single narrow band of sharpness with symmetric blur ramps, (c) colour and contrast lifted past reality so surfaces look like painted plastic. Those three traits are the recipe; no named photographer, film or artist is required.

Silhouette rule: masses must be blocky and separable from above — roofs, containers, vehicles and tree crowns read as distinct rounded-rectangular tops with 1.5-3 m gaps between them; a scene that overlaps into one continuous roof plane cannot be saved by focus.

Scale cues run the opposite way here: keep real-world dimensions honest (door 2.0 m, bus 12 m, container 6.1 m, lane 3.2 m) so the eye's only evidence for 'model' is the optics — a fake-miniature look built by shrinking objects reads as a broken scene, not a diorama.

Aerial haze is deliberately absent. Depth separation comes from the focus ramp, hard cast shadows and the 1.5-3 m gaps between masses, so this look intentionally opts out of the usual fog requirement and says so.
implementation: Camera: 22° vertical FOV (telephoto), 45 m height, -38° pitch, orbit clamped to 25-55° polar and 40-120 m distance. Wide lenses restore full-size perspective cues and kill the effect.

Depth of field: focus distance 60 m at an f/1.4 equivalent aperture; the fully sharp band spans 20% of frame height (acceptable range 18-25%), and the blur ramps symmetrically to a 12 px circle of confusion at the top and bottom edges at 1080p. Scale the CoC target with output height so a 4K render keeps the same apparent falloff.
Colour grade: lift global saturation +18% and contrast +10% over the physically plausible values; the hero accent (#d94f3d) is allowed 80% saturation while everything non-focal stays at or below 55%.
Sun: DirectionalLight #fff6e2 at 3.4, elevation 58°, azimuth 140°, castShadow true, shadow map 2048 with normalBias 0.03 — high sun and hard, short shadows are how models are lit on a table.

Materials: a moulded-plastic finish — roughness 0.35-0.5 on vehicles with clearcoat 0.15, 0.6-0.8 on ground and roofs, and every edge bevelled at 2-3 mm so it catches a highlight. Suppress detail below 5 cm: seams, small text and micro-scratches break the toy read.
Motion: move vehicles and figures at 0.6-0.8× plausible speed with a hold of 250 ms at stops and a linear ease — smooth realistic easing reads as full-size, slightly mechanical timing reads as model.
observable_checks: Measure the sharp band in the rendered frame: 18-25% of frame height, and the hero sits inside it.
Blur monotonicity: sample circle-of-confusion at 10%, 30%, 50%, 70% and 90% of frame height — it must fall to a minimum inside the band and rise on both sides.
Disable the DOF pass: the frame should immediately read as an ordinary aerial photograph. If it still looks miniature, the geometry has been shrunk instead of the optics changed.
Check the saturation histogram: the non-focal peak sits at or below 55% while at least one accent region exceeds 70%.

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for ACESFilmic tone mapping at renderer.toneMappingExposure 1.0 with three.js physically-based light units; re-tune every intensity under AgX, Neutral or a different exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: The band can be tilted off horizontal by up to 15° to follow a road or quay; keep it a single band, since two focus zones destroy the read.
Night variants work if the practicals stay hard-edged: keep the DOF band, drop the key to 0.4 and let street lamps at 30-60 candela with decay 2 carry the frame.
Subject is free — rail yards, market squares, construction sites, airports — as long as the masses stay separable from above.

defaults.rationale: Every number here serves one perceptual trick: a real camera close to a small object has a shallow depth of field, so simulating that falloff at a 60 m focus distance with an f/1.4-equivalent aperture and a 20%-of-frame-height sharp band convinces the eye the subject is centimetres across. The 22° FOV and 45 m height remove wide-angle perspective divergence that would betray full scale, the +18% saturation and +10% contrast imitate painted model surfaces, and fog is set to none on purpose because aerial haze is a full-size depth cue that directly fights the illusion.

palette.role: pavement and roofs — dominant light mid
hero accent (bus, one roof, a crane)

values.value_structure: 25/55/20 dark/mid/light; the sharp band holds the two highest-contrast elements in the frame
values.saturation_rule: global saturation lifted +18% over plausible reality; non-focal ≤ 55% HSL, hero accent ≤ 80%

lights.ratio: key:fill ≈ 5:1 — hard, short shadows are what sunlight on a tabletop model looks like

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

materials.notes: moulded-plastic finish: vehicles roughness 0.35-0.5 with clearcoat 0.15, ground and roofs 0.6-0.8; 2-3 mm bevel on every visible edge so it catches a highlight; suppress all detail below 5 cm

post.dof: on: focus distance 60 m, f/1.4 equivalent, sharp band 20% of frame height (18-25%), symmetric ramp reaching a 12 px circle of confusion at the top and bottom edges at 1080p

values.signature_technique: A horizontal sharp band of 18-25% of frame height with symmetric blur ramps above and below, plus a +18% saturation and +10% contrast lift — the viewer infers scale from focus falloff, never from object size.
never: fog or aerial haze (it restores full-size depth cues)
uniform blur across the whole frame
photoreal detail density on figures and vehicles
